```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", eval = FALSE)
```

This guide crosses two surveys of 2024: monetary poverty from ENAHO and the share of women among
agricultural producers from ENA, both by department, and maps them. The code does not run when
the vignette is built, because it needs the INEI files (about 150 MB for the two modules) and the
INEI boundaries (9 MB); `faperu` downloads them to its cache the first time.

## 1. One estimate with its precision

```{r}
library(faperu)
library(faperu.analysis)

s <- fa_read("enaho", 2024, "34", file = "Sumaria-2024\\.")
s$poor <- s$pobreza %in% 1:2
s$w <- s$factor07 * s$mieperho          # poverty counts people, not households
d <- fa_design(s, "enaho", weight = "w")
fpa_estimate(d, "poor", type = "prop")
```

`fpa_estimate()` gives the estimate (27.6%), its standard error, a 95% interval, the coefficient
of variation and the INEI quality band: below 5% "muy buena", up to 10% "buena", up to 15%
"aceptable", above that "referencial". `by` takes `"department"`, `"area"`, `"district"` or any
column of the data.

## 2. Ready indicators

The same number comes ready, by department:

```{r}
fpa_indicators()
poverty <- fpa_indicator("pobreza_monetaria", 2024, by = "department")
women <- fpa_indicator("mujeres_productoras", 2024, by = "department")
```

Each ready indicator was checked against the figure INEI published for 2024. With the files of
the INEI microdata portal the package gives:

| Indicator | Survey | INEI 2024 | faperu.analysis |
|---|---|---|---|
| Monetary poverty (urban, rural) | ENAHO | 27.6 (24.8, 39.3) | 27.58 (24.81, 39.30) |
| Extreme poverty | ENAHO | 5.5 | 5.50 |
| Open unemployment | EPEN | 5.6 | 5.57 |
| Informal employment | EPEN | 70.9 | 70.95 |
| Anaemia 6-35 months, WHO 2024 (urban, rural) | ENDES | 35.3 (31.2, 44.7) | 35.33 (31.23, 44.65) |
| Anaemia 6-35 months, RM 363-2022 (urban, rural) | ENDES | 43.7 (40.2, 51.9) | 43.74 (40.17, 51.85) |
| Women among producers | ENA | 31.5 | 31.46 |

The sources are in `fpa_indicators()$source`. The package tests repeat these checks whenever the
files are on disk.

## 3. A table for the paper

```{r}
cat(fpa_table(poverty, format = "markdown", caption = "Monetary poverty by department, 2024 (%)"),
    sep = "\n")
```

Departments whose CV is above 15% (Ica, Madre de Dios and Moquegua for poverty in 2024) carry an
asterisk and a note. `format = "latex"` gives the same table for LaTeX.

## 4. Linking the two surveys

```{r}
both <- fpa_link(poverty = poverty, women = women)
head(both)
cor(both$estimate_poverty, both$estimate_women)
```

`fpa_link()` joins by department code and year. It warns when an estimate is "referencial",
so a correlation does not lean on numbers INEI would not publish without a caveat. With
`level = "district"` the codes are first moved to the 2017 Census frame with `fa_ubigeo()`;
districts created after 2017 join the district they split from, and the two that split from
several districts (Lambras and Santa Lucia) are left out with a warning.

## 5. Maps

```{r}
fpa_map(both, "estimate_poverty", title = "Monetary poverty, 2024")
fpa_map(both, "estimate_women", title = "Women among agricultural producers, 2024")
```

The boundaries are the department layer of INEI's spatial data infrastructure
(<https://ide.inei.gob.pe/>), downloaded once to `fa_cache()/GEO`. `fpa_geometry("district")`
gives the 1890 districts of the current layer; `fpa_map(..., level = "district", base = 2017)`
merges them into the 2017 frame used by `fpa_link()`.

Both maps return `ggplot` objects, so titles, themes and `ggplot2::ggsave()` work as usual.
